newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Virgin Express says shunning cargo traffic.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Express says shunning cargo traffic.

text.p: Richard Branson's Virgin Express low-cost regional airline said on Thursday it had no plans to develop its cargo business and would concentrate on passenger traffic.

"We fly a little cargo, primarily between London and Brussels, but it is not an area that I'm really trying to develop. We like to be a passenger airline, we take cargo when it shows up," chief executive officer Jonathan Ornstein told Reuters in an interview.
"We do about a million dollars a year in cargo business, it's a very small piece," he added.
Ornstein said he was happy just filling up the cabin portion of the airplane and leaving the cargo hold empty for now.
He said people usually saw cargo business as easily-won added revenue but often overlooked the costs.
"The costs sometimes are costs you don't see like holding a plane for a cargo shipment, or the cargo truck smacks the airplane and the plane is down for a day, it happens a lot," Ornstein said.
